messages.author: f17ec5a3936c7373
messages.subject: trouble parsing cholesky_factor_cov
parts:
Here is my entire transformed data block:

transformed data {
  cholesky_factor_cov[num_strains] strain_mef_add_chol;
  strain_mef_add_chol = cholesky_decompose(strain_mef_add_covar);
  
  cholesky_factor_cov[num_strains] strain_vef_add_chol;
  strain_vef_add_chol = cholesky_decompose(strain_vef_add_covar);
}


I am getting the error:

SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:

variable "cholesky_factor_cov" does not exist.

ERROR at line 22

 20:      strain_mef_add_chol = cholesky_decompose(strain_mef_add_covar);
 21:      
 22:      cholesky_factor_cov[num_strains] strain_vef_add_chol;
                             ^
 23:      strain_vef_add_chol = cholesky_decompose(strain_vef_add_covar);



And here's the relevant subset of the data block:

data {
 
  ...

  cov_matrix[num_strains] strain_mef_add_covar;

  cov_matrix[num_strains] strain_vef_add_covar;
}


It seems the parser is interpreting the type of 'strain_vef_add_chol' as if it were a variable name?  Maybe I've made a syntax error that I'm not seeing?


Robert Corty

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] trouble parsing cholesky_factor_cov
parts:
Hi Robert,

All the declarations need to be at the top of the block. You can't have statements between declarations.

For future reference, please include the whole program when you ask for help. It's a lot easier to help when you provide the full program. And I understand... most people think they're doing the users list favors by only pasting in parts of programs. It's not -- it makes it much harder to debug.


Daniel

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] trouble parsing cholesky_factor_cov
parts:
It's also hard to have a more informative error message here because, informally, it thinks declarations are over once you've made that first assignment and therefore interprets your attempted declaration as a variable name.

Although maybe in this case because you're using cholesky_factor_cov it should know it can't be a variable and could throw a different error (Daniel I assume that's harder than it sounds?).

Either way, unfortunately I think it would be hard to have an error that told you that the problem was that you need to declare everything at the top of the block.

Jonah

You can also do it this way:

{

cholesky_factor_cov[num_strains] strain_vef_add_chol;
strain_vef_add_chol = cholesky_decompose(strain_vef_add_covar);
}

When you add braces, you can declare new variables.

- Bob

the chapter Statements, which mentions this property
in the very first paragraph and then goes into details
in the section "Statement Blocks and Local Variable Declarations".
